analysis.title: Global Technology: Opportunities in a volatile market
key_insights: Portfolio manager Hyun Ho Sohn says the FF Global Technology Fund has outperformed in recent volatility, helped by an underweight in large-cap AI semiconductor names and select positions in software and IT services.

Volatility over the last few months is attributed to concern about the sustainability of AI capex given deteriorating cash flows at big spenders, rising interest rates raising the cost of capex (hitting second-tier companies such as neoclouds), and a quick unwind of crowded AI capex positioning that de-rated hardware and semiconductor stocks.
Fund 1-month return is 0.3% vs -6.2% for MSCI ACWI Information Technology (N). Year to date the fund returned 20.3% vs 31.3% for the index, so it remains behind the benchmark.
Underweights in Apple and Microsoft detracted, as the market has treated these stocks as safe havens.

Sohn expects tightening funding to make it hard for AI capex to keep growing at its recent pace and stays cautious on related plays. Hyperscaler equity and debt issuance is crowding out neoclouds that need external capital, and he cites widening credit spreads and failed neocloud IPOs.

In the latest earnings season most hyperscalers did not raise capex guidance as in prior quarters, and some neoclouds cut capex plans or turned cautious on next year's growth. He calls this a complete change in tone.

He remains positive on hyperscalers. He favors Amazon (AWS proprietary compute, sticky customer base, high-margin inference), sees Alphabet's de-rating as a fixable Search monetisation issue with cloud value and external TPU sales as added growth, and recently increased Meta on Meta Muse.
He is significantly underweight semiconductors, arguing the sector is cyclical, many companies are over-earning after the AI capex run, and the best time to own them is when demand is weak.
Semiconductor exposure is selective: analog (Texas Instruments, which built automated in-house capacity) and a modest overweight in European equipment names including ASML.

In software he is selective and valuation-sensitive. He owns names with high switching costs, AI monetisation potential and cheap valuations, calling Oracle mispriced (AI data centre concerns overblown) and favoring Intuit.
IT services trade at historical trough valuations. He prefers Accenture for execution and its role in enterprise AI deployment.

The fund is overweight China (e-commerce, travel, property transactions, recruitment, domestic semiconductors), has added cybersecurity and data centre stocks after weakness, and sees Netflix and Spotify as more resilient to AI disruption.

He expects 2027 to be another volatile year for tech. Risks are elevated AI spending, supply disruptions, tightening financing, rising equity supply from raises and IPOs, and expectations for continued strong AI capex.

market_movers.rationale: Seen as a long-term winner in retail and cloud. AWS has proprietary compute, a large sticky customer base and a focus on high-margin inference.
De-rating on Search concerns is seen as a temporary, fixable monetisation issue. Cloud has full-stack AI compute and TPUs are now sold externally.
Position recently increased. Meta Muse shows innovation and monetisation potential beyond core advertising.
Analog name with a higher-quality, diversified model. Automated in-house manufacturing capacity is paying off in the current cycle.
Modest overweight in European semiconductor equipment. Strong competitive position and attractive valuation.
Seen as mispriced. Core products are sticky and concern about its AI data centre business is viewed as overblown.
Strong potential to monetise AI at a very attractive valuation, despite AI disruption risk in its small and medium-sized business exposure.
Trades cheaply as the market focuses on AI disruption risk. Consulting and implementation capability positions it for enterprise AI adoption.
Seen as resilient to AI disruption and macro sensitivity. Products are consumer utilities with scaled distribution that AI should help.

The fund is underweight. The stock has acted as a safe haven in the recent volatility, which weighed on relative performance.

sector_views.rationale: Cyclical sector with companies over-earning after the AI capex run. Exceptions are analog and European equipment names.
Selective and valuation-sensitive. Prefers names with high switching costs, AI monetisation potential and cheap valuations.
Valuations are at historical troughs, but the fund prefers names with execution confidence such as Accenture.
Well positioned for profitable long-term growth from AI adoption, with full-stack offerings beyond commoditised compute.
Stocks are under-earning in a weak macro environment but have strong fundamentals, cheap valuations and improving shareholder returns.
Seen as more resilient to AI disruption and macro conditions, with scaled distribution platforms.

earnings_insights: Most hyperscalers did not raise capex guidance in the latest earnings season, unlike in prior quarters.
Some neocloud companies explicitly cut capex plans and others turned cautious on next year's capex growth.
risk_factors: Elevated level of AI spending and deteriorating cash flows at big spenders.
Rising interest rates and tightening funding conditions, particularly for neoclouds, with widening credit spreads and failed neocloud IPOs.
Increasing stock supply through equity raises and IPOs.
Market expectations for continued strong AI capex.
AI disruption risk to software and IT services businesses.
vol_and_positioning: Investors heavily positioned in AI capex beneficiaries unwound positions quickly, causing a sharp de-rating of hardware and semiconductor stocks exposed to the AI theme.
The fund's underweight in large-cap AI semiconductor names was the largest positive contributor as AI trades reversed.
Apple and Microsoft have been treated as safe havens in the recent volatility.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are well positioned for profitable long-term AI-driven growth with full-stack offerings, and AI adoption keeps driving demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Tightening funding, widening credit spreads, failed neocloud IPOs, flat hyperscaler capex guidance and neocloud capex cuts make continued strong capex growth difficult.

theme_stances.key_argument: Tightening funding will make it difficult for AI capex to continue growing at its recent pace.
theme_stances.evidence: tightening funding environment will make it difficult for AI capex to continue growing

theme_stances.key_argument: Many semiconductor companies are over-earning after the AI capex tailwind, and the market under-appreciates the sector's cyclicality.
Hyperscalers provide comprehensive AI solutions beyond commoditised compute and are positioned for profitable long-term growth.
theme_stances.evidence: well positioned to enjoy profitable long-term growth driven by AI adoption
